prompt.context: Our client, a private equity firm, is considering purchasing Kiki's Coffee. Kiki's started off with a few stores on the West Coast where it did quite well. As the demand for coffee shops rose over the past decade, it decided to expand throughout the country.
prompt.question: Should our private equity client purchase Kiki's Coffee?

clarifying_info.q: Where is Kiki's positioned in the market?
clarifying_info.a: Kiki's is positioned on the higher end and focuses on quality coffee beans, but does not sell all the extras (CDs, etc.) that Starbucks sells.
Starbucks is the market leader and paved the way for this large market. Although the market is still growing, it is probably getting somewhat saturated over time.

exhibits.title: Stores Nationwide and Revenues 2004–2007
exhibits.shows: Two charts: (1) number of stores nationwide from 2004 to 2007; (2) total revenues in millions from 2004 to 2007.

exhibits.title: Revenue per Store (Calculated Table) 2004–2007
exhibits.shows: A table showing year, total revenue, number of stores, and revenue per store for 2004–2007, plus context on key insight about declining revenue per store.

exhibits.title: Cost Structure and Per-Store Cost Trends 2004–2007
exhibits.shows: Four charts: (1) total costs broken into Cost of Sales, D&A, Rent and Labor, and Operating Profit; (2) CAGR trends; (3) Labor/store over time; (4) Rent/store over time. Shows that operating profit is growing in absolute terms but cost of sales is growing faster.

data.operating_profit_trend: increasing in absolute dollars but margins shrinking

framework: Market analysis: size, growth rate, saturation level, competitive landscape (Starbucks as leader)
Company analysis: positioning (premium quality coffee), geographic expansion history, store count growth
Revenue analysis: total revenue growth vs. revenue per store trend
Cost analysis: cost of sales, D&A, rent, labor — both absolute and per-store
Profitability/margins: operating profit trend and margin compression
Investment attractiveness: whether the PE firm should acquire

questions.prompt: What do the two charts (Exhibit 1) indicate about Kiki's growth?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies that store count is growing steadily (30 to 100 stores, 2004–2007) and total revenues are rising ($110m to $200m). But the candidate should calculate revenue per store to identify the key tension: revenue per store is declining even as total revenue grows. This suggests new stores are underperforming relative to existing ones.

math.setup: Revenue per store = Total Revenue / Number of Stores for each year
math.answer: Revenue per store has fallen from $3.7m in 2004 to $2.0m in 2007 — nearly halved in three years.

questions.prompt: What other financial information should we review after seeing the revenue trend?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that even though revenue per store is falling, costs may also be decreasing as the chain scales, which could preserve or increase profits. The next step is to examine costs and margins.

questions.prompt: What do you think Kiki's main costs are?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) cost of ingredients/coffee beans (cost of sales), (2) property rental costs, (3) labor costs. D&A is also relevant. Ideally candidate lists these before seeing Exhibit 3.

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 3 (cost and margin charts) tell you?
questions.guidance: Operating profit is increasing in absolute terms, but cost of sales is growing even faster than revenues. As a result, profit margins are decreasing. Cost per store for both labor and rent is declining (potential scale benefit or cheaper real estate in expansion markets), but this improvement is not enough to offset the severe revenue-per-store decline. Net conclusion: margins are shrinking.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some ways Kiki's might be able to increase revenue per store?

categories.name: New products
ideas: Expand into food items such as muffins and fruit

categories.name: Product mix optimization
ideas: Review current drink offerings to ensure alignment with local tastes
Adjust menu based on regional preferences in new markets

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Determine whether prices can be raised and by how much
Test premium pricing in high-demand locations

categories.name: In-store sales effectiveness
ideas: Train staff to upsell customers more effectively
Improve speed of service to increase throughput

categories.name: Customer retention
ideas: Launch a loyalty program to increase visit frequency

categories.name: Local partnerships
ideas: Sell goods from local retailers within new market stores
Partner with local food producers to differentiate menu

recommendation: Kiki's Coffee is an attractive acquisition target for the private equity client.
It has steadily grown revenues and successfully expanded its store base nationally in a growing market.
While profit margins are declining due to falling revenue per store, several strategies exist to reverse this trend.
risks: Revenue per store has nearly halved from 2004 to 2007, suggesting new stores are significantly underperforming legacy stores.
The coffee shop market is becoming increasingly saturated; Starbucks dominates and further expansion may face headwinds.
Margin compression may continue if new-store ramp-up issues are not resolved.
next_steps: Investigate root cause of revenue-per-store decline (new store locations, cannibalization, weaker markets).
Model the impact of revenue improvement levers (new products, loyalty programs, repricing).
Assess whether the acquisition price reflects the current margin pressure or assumes a successful turnaround.
